Apple updated TestFlight this week, adding support for landscape orientation mode, as well as support for resizable iPhone mirroring windows in macOS 27 Golden Gate. Details below.

TestFlight now supports landscape orientation mode on iOS

Apple earlier this month launched macOS 27 Golden Gate, which supports resizing the iPhone mirroring window with additional aspect ratios.

When this feature first debuted in macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 1, many speculated it was clearly paving the way for Apple's long-rumoured foldable iPhone.

At the iPhone Duo launch event, Apple said it had adapted every native iOS app to the various orientations of the device's inner and outer screens, making the connection even more apparent.

Apple also updated TestFlight this week, adding support for landscape orientation mode, as well as the additional aspect ratios introduced with the iPhone mirroring feature in macOS 27 Golden Gate.

Here are the updates in TestFlight version 4.4.0:

Landscape orientation mode on iPhone. Resizable window when using iPhone mirroring on Mac with devices running OS 27 or later (available in supported countries and regions). Stability improvements and bug fixes.

In landscape mode, TestFlight switches from the original single-column app list to a two-column layout. The app details page also makes better use of the extra horizontal space, displaying the app and developer information panels side by side below "What's New", "Preview" and "App Description".

iPhone Duo will be available for pre-order starting October 16, with official sales beginning October 23. US pricing starts at US$1,999, featuring a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch foldable inner display.
